  have h4ne : thetaFour τ ≠ 0 := thetaFour_ne_zero_of_im_pos hτ

# Prime--archimedean centered Eisenstein residual RH law

- **ID:** `prime-arch-centered-eisenstein-residual-rh`
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** `[BRIDGE] [LEAN-PROVED] [RIGHT-EDGE HYPOTHESIS REDUCTION] [NOT RH]`
- **Parents:** `prime-arch-centered-analytic-tail-vacuum-cone`,
  `prime-arch-theta-hankel-degree-tail`
- **Claim:** For every infinite degree set `D`, target normalized-variance nonnegativity is
  RH-complete after simultaneously restricting to strict centered analytic-tail residuals and to
  vacuum tails of monic integer polynomials Eisenstein at `2` whose exact degrees lie in `D`.

## Exact statement

For `P in Z[X]`, let

```text
tail(P) = P - C(P(0)),
Residual(q) := 8 |E_PG(q)| < tailL1(q).
```

Define

```text
CenteredTwoEisensteinResidualVarianceNonnegative(D) :=
  for every P in Z[X],
    Monic(P) -> EisensteinAt(2,P) -> degree(P) in D ->
    Residual(tail(P)) ->
    Var_PG(tail(P)) >= 0.
```

Then, for every infinite `D subseteq N`,

```text
CenteredTwoEisensteinResidualVarianceNonnegative(D) <-> RH.      (E1)
```

Consequently, if RH is false, every infinite `D` contains the exact degree of a monic
`2`-Eisenstein polynomial `P` whose zero-constant vacuum tail satisfies

```text
Residual(tail(P)),
Var_PG(tail(P)) < 0.                                            (E2)
```

Let `BadDeg` be the set of degrees admitting such a `P`. Then `(E2)` has the sharp cofinite form

```text
not RH -> Finite(N \\ BadDeg).                                  (E2c)
```

Thus failure is not represented by one exceptional polynomial degree: every sufficiently large
degree carries a structured negative centered witness.

The coupled-Sonin normalized-variance comparison is therefore needed only on these structured
residual tails for any one chosen infinite degree set.

## Dependency-closed paper proof

Assume `D` is infinite and `(E1)`'s left side. The corpus theorem
`primeArchSourceTraceHankelIntTwoEisensteinDegreeSetNonnegative_iff_riemannHypothesis`

# The Xi null vector for spectral Schwartz forms

This file joins the constructive spectral-measure form with the Xi support theorem.  If an actual
Schwartz source has Fourier transform `XiC` on the real axis, then nullity of that source forces
the spectral measure to be the sum of its atoms at the real Xi zeros.  Integrability is discharged
from Schwartz decay and temperate growth; it is not an extra hypothesis.
-/

open Complex Function MeasureTheory
open scoped FourierTransform SchwartzMap

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- The squared Xi norm is integrable against every temperate spectral measure once it is realized
as the Fourier transform of a Schwartz source. -/
theorem integrable_xiRealNormSq_of_fourier_eq_XiC
    (μ : Measure ℝ) [μ.HasTemperateGrowth]
    (k : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) (hk : ∀ t : ℝ, 𝓕 k t = XiC (t : ℂ)) :
    Integrable xiRealNormSq μ := by
  let h : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ) := SchwartzMap.pointwiseMulConj
    ((SchwartzMap.fourierTransformCLM ℂ) k)
    ((SchwartzMap.fourierTransformCLM ℂ) k)
  have hint : Integrable h μ := h.integrable
  exact hint.re.congr (by
    filter_upwards with t
    change (h t).re = xiRealNormSq t
    simp [h, hk, xiRealNormSq, Complex.mul_conj, Complex.sq_norm])

/-- Exact Xi energy formula for the spectral form of a Schwartz theta source. -/
theorem spectralMeasureForm_self_eq_integral_xiRealNormSq
    (μ : Measure ℝ) [μ.HasTemperateGrowth]
    (k : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) (hk : ∀ t : ℝ, 𝓕 k t = XiC (t : ℂ)) :
    SchwartzMap.spectralMeasureForm μ k k =
      ∫ t, (xiRealNormSq t : ℂ) ∂μ := by
  rw [SchwartzMap.spectralMeasureForm_apply]
  apply integral_congr_ae
  filter_upwards with t
  rw [hk]
  simp [xiRealNormSq, Complex.mul_conj, Complex.sq_norm]

/-- A null Schwartz source with Fourier transform `XiC` forces the complete atomic Xi-zero
decomposition of its temperate spectral measure. -/
theorem spectralMeasure_eq_sum_smul_dirac_xiRealZeroSet_of_null_source
    (μ : Measure ℝ) [μ.HasTemperateGrowth]
    (k : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) (hk : ∀ t : ℝ, 𝓕 k t = XiC (t : ℂ))
    (hnull : SchwartzMap.spectralMeasureForm μ k k = 0) :
    μ = Measure.sum
      (fun t : xiRealZeroSet => μ {(t : ℝ)} • Measure.dirac (t : ℝ)) := by
  have hint := integrable_xiRealNormSq_of_fourier_eq_XiC μ k hk
  apply measure_eq_sum_smul_dirac_xiRealZeroSet_of_integral_normSq_eq_zero μ hint
  have hcomplex : (∫ t, (xiRealNormSq t : ℂ) ∂μ) = 0 := by
    rw [← spectralMeasureForm_self_eq_integral_xiRealNormSq μ k hk]
    exact hnull
  rw [integral_complex_ofReal] at hcomplex
  exact_mod_cast hcomplex

end

/-!
# Suzuki cross-parity spectral-pair transport

The finite parity transport budget must be stated on the literal source spectral measures of
Suzuki's restricted-Weil operator. This module supplies that measure-level carrier.

For even node `t`, odd node `s`, source weights `a,b`, and a shift below the spectrum, the exact
cross-parity kernel is

`a b (s-t) / ((t-lambda)^2 (s-lambda)^2)`.

Fubini factorization proves that its product-measure integral is exactly the cross-Wronskian
`E' O - E O'`. After normalization it is the parity hazard `E'/E-O'/O`. Its positive and
negative parts therefore have a literal meaning: lower-even-pair credit and odd-below-even
spectral-inversion debt. Positive transport occurs exactly when credit exceeds debt. This allows
arbitrarily many local spectral reversals and makes no global monotone-likelihood assumption.

The product-integral algebra is classical. Its role is to expose the exact infinite spectral
quantity that the Suzuki prime--archimedean source must control. No Riemann-hypothesis assumption
or numerical computation occurs.
-/

variable {α β : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] [MeasurableSpace β]

/-- Stieltjes energy of one weighted source spectral measure. -/
def suzukiParitySpectralEnergy
    (μ : Measure α) (node weight : α → ℝ) (lambda : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x, weight x * suzukiShiftResolventKernel node lambda x ∂μ

/-- Squared-resolvent velocity of one weighted source spectral measure. -/
def suzukiParitySquaredSpectralEnergy
    (μ : Measure α) (node weight : α → ℝ) (lambda : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x, weight x * suzukiShiftResolventKernel node lambda x ^ 2 ∂μ

/-- Pointwise signed odd-minus-even spectral-gap contribution. -/
def suzukiParitySpectralCrossGapKernel
    (evenNode evenWeight : α → ℝ) (oddNode oddWeight : β → ℝ)
    (lambda : ℝ) (z : α × β) : ℝ :=
  evenWeight z.1 * oddWeight z.2 * (oddNode z.2 - evenNode z.1) /
    ((evenNode z.1 - lambda) ^ 2 * (oddNode z.2 - lambda) ^ 2)

/-- Total signed cross-parity spectral-gap mass. -/

    (μ : Measure α) (ν : Measure β)
    (evenNode evenWeight : α → ℝ) (oddNode oddWeight : β → ℝ)
    (lambda : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ z, suzukiParitySpectralCrossGapKernel
    evenNode evenWeight oddNode oddWeight lambda z ∂μ.prod ν

    (μ : Measure α) (ν : Measure β)

    (lambda : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  suzukiParitySquaredSpectralEnergy μ evenNode evenWeight lambda /
      suzukiParitySpectralEnergy μ evenNode evenWeight lambda -
    suzukiParitySquaredSpectralEnergy ν oddNode oddWeight lambda /
      suzukiParitySpectralEnergy ν oddNode oddWeight lambda

def suzukiParitySpectralLowerPairCredit
    (μ : Measure α) (ν : Measure β)
    (evenNode evenWeight : α → ℝ) (oddNode oddWeight : β → ℝ)
    (lambda : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ z, (suzukiParitySpectralCrossGapKernel
    evenNode evenWeight oddNode oddWeight lambda z)⁺ ∂μ.prod ν

    (μ : Measure α) (ν : Measure β)
    (evenNode evenWeight : α → ℝ) (oddNode oddWeight : β → ℝ)
    (lambda : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ z, (suzukiParitySpectralCrossGapKernel
    evenNode evenWeight oddNode oddWeight lambda z)⁻ ∂μ.prod ν

    integral_map (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)]

theorem norm_charFun_eq_one_iff_phase_locked
    (μ : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (t : ℝ) :
    ‖charFun μ t‖ = 1 ↔
      ∃ c : ℂ, ‖c‖ = 1 ∧ spectralPhase t =ᵐ[μ] const ℝ c := by

    rcases spectralPhase_ae_eq_const_or_norm_charFun_lt_one μ t with h | h

      rw [charFun_apply_real]
      simp_rw [← Complex.ofReal_mul]

    (μ : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {t : ℝ} (ht : t ≠ 0) (hreturn : ‖charFun μ t‖ = 1) :
    ∃ s : Set ℝ, s.Countable ∧ μ s = 1 := by
  obtain ⟨c, _hc, hae⟩ :=
    (norm_charFun_eq_one_iff_phase_locked μ t).mp hreturn
  let s : Set ℝ := {x : ℝ | spectralPhase t x = c}

  have haes : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ s := by
    simpa [s, EventuallyEq, const] using hae

at every nonzero time. -/

    (μ : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [NullSingletonClass μ]
    {t : ℝ} (ht : t ≠ 0) :

  have hreturn : ‖charFun μ t‖ = 1 :=
    le_antisymm (norm_charFun_le_one t) (not_lt.mp hnot)
  obtain ⟨s, hs, hmass⟩ :=
    exact_return_has_countable_spectral_carrier μ ht hreturn
  have hzero : μ s = 0 := hs.measure_zero μ
  rw [hzero] at hmass
  norm_num at hmass

exactly at a nonzero time, every atomless submeasure is zero.  Thus any
continuous component, however small, forbids exact return. -/
theorem exact_return_has_no_atomless_submeasure
    (μ ν : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [NullSingletonClass ν]
    {t : ℝ} (ht : t ≠ 0) (hreturn : ‖charFun μ t‖ = 1)
    (hνμ : ν ≤ μ) :
    ν = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨s, hs, hmass⟩ :=
    exact_return_has_countable_spectral_carrier μ ht hreturn
  have hμcomp : μ sᶜ = 0 := by
    rw [measure_compl hs.measurableSet (by finiteness), hmass]
    simp
  have hνs : ν s = 0 := hs.measure_zero ν
  have hνcomp : ν sᶜ = 0 :=
    le_antisymm ((hνμ (sᶜ)).trans_eq hμcomp) (by simp)
  rw [← Measure.measure_univ_eq_zero]
  calc
    ν Set.univ = ν (s ∪ sᶜ) := by rw [union_compl_self]
    _ = ν s + ν sᶜ :=
      measure_union disjoint_compl_right hs.measurableSet.compl
    _ = 0 := by rw [hνs, hνcomp, add_zero]
